questions.prompt: What is your enterprise position on owned and leased data centre facilities?
questions.hint: Considers contractual lease expirations, colocation commitments, and board-mandated exit timelines.

options.text: No formal posture; decisions occur ad-hoc at lease renewal deadlines
Broad cloud-first mandate exists, but facility exits lack mapped dependencies and dates
Evaluating per-facility disposition (exit, consolidate, colocate, or retain)
Structured DC exit underway with identified target migration waves
Disciplined hybrid estate: selected DCs optimized as strategic assets alongside cloud

questions.prompt: Which facility and infrastructure asset classes are currently tracked in automated discovery?
questions.hint: Select all that apply across your physical, virtual, and power topologies.

options.text: Physical Compute & Hypervisors (Bare-metal, VMware, Nutanix)
Storage & SAN Fabrics (Block, File, Object, Backup arrays)
Network Topologies & Top-of-Rack Switches
Power Distribution Units (PDUs) & Sub-metered Breaker Loads
Shadow Data Centre & Edge Server Rooms (Branch/Plant closets)

questions.prompt: Rate your contract runway risk regarding upcoming facility leases or OEM hardware refresh cliffs:
questions.hint: 1 = Severe immediate cliff (<6 months); 5 = Fully decoupled runway with zero contractual lock-in.

questions.prompt: Estimated peak power utilization relative to utility substation allocated capacity:
questions.hint: Over 68% of enterprise data centres hit utility breaker or transformer limits before floor space limits.

questions.prompt: What is your facility thermal cooling architecture's capability for modern rack densities?
questions.hint: Traditional CRAC/CRAH handles 5–10 kW/rack; modern AI clusters demand 30–100+ kW/rack.

options.text: Legacy air cooling struggling with standard racks (>5–7 kW causes hot spots)
Standard hot/cold aisle containment supporting up to 10–12 kW/rack maximum
High-density hybrid zones engineered for 15–25 kW/rack in designated rows
Rear-door heat exchangers or in-row liquid assist operational for 30–50 kW/rack
Direct-to-chip liquid cooling or immersion infrastructure in production for >70 kW/rack

questions.prompt: Rate your facility energy efficiency governance and PUE (Power Usage Effectiveness) telemetry:
questions.hint: 1 = PUE unmeasured (>1.9); 5 = Sub-metered audited real-time PUE (<1.25) with renewable PPAs.

questions.prompt: Where and how is high-density AI/GPU compute capacity planned and sited?
questions.hint: Addresses the critical dilemma: public cloud vs specialized colocation vs retrofitting owned DCs.

options.text: No plan; business units order cloud GPUs or shadow workstations without central architecture
Assuming 100% of AI will run in hyperscaler public cloud regardless of latency/data volume
Evaluating AI siting tradeoffs (data residency, inference latency, power cost, and sovereignty)
Structured hybrid AI siting framework: training in public cloud, low-latency inference on-prem/colo
Optimized multi-tier AI topology: high-density sovereign clusters matched to exact workload envelopes

questions.prompt: AI Workload Siting Matrix: Map current or planned deployment targets across key AI archetypes:
questions.hint: Evaluates how data gravity and sovereignty dictate compute placement.

questions.prompt: How are data residency and technical sovereignty governed for proprietary enterprise AI data?
questions.hint: Prevents regulatory non-compliance under EU AI Act, DORA, DPDP, and SEC disclosure rules.

options.text: Unmanaged; proprietary enterprise data exposed to public SaaS/AI models
Informal policy prohibiting sensitive data in public AI, but technical controls lacking
Clear classification of AI data domains with private tenancy agreements in public cloud
Sovereign AI enclaves: air-gapped or dedicated hardware for regulated PII and IP
Cryptographically enforced zero-trust AI pipelines with localized model inference

questions.prompt: Percentage of application portfolio with an officially approved 6R modernization disposition:
questions.hint: The 6 R's: Rehost, Replatform, Refactor, Repurchase (SaaS), Retain, Retire.

questions.prompt: How dominant are legacy monolithic dependencies and technical debt in your estate?
questions.hint: Includes mainframes, legacy Unix/AIX, unsupported databases, and tightly coupled batch jobs.

options.text: Estate dominated by aging monoliths (>70%) with severe documentation deficits
Heavy monolith footprint (40%–70%) creating complex migration blast radiuses
Moderate footprint (20%–40%); modern tiers separated from legacy core engines
Low footprint (<20%); legacy systems encapsulated behind API mediation layers
Decoupled cloud-native estate; legacy systems retired or replatformed into microservices

questions.prompt: Prioritize your enterprise modernization drivers (Drag or use arrows to rank 1 to 4):
questions.hint: Top-ranked items directly shape your tailored advisory roadmap priorities.

questions.prompt: Do you operate a repeatable, industrialized migration factory with proven velocity?
questions.hint: Assesses automation, standardized runbooks, cutover testing, and predictable delivery throughput.

options.text: No repeatable factory; every application migration is treated as a bespoke project
Documented guidelines exist, but migrations require extensive manual engineering
Documented playbooks with standardized landing templates and wave scheduling
Automated migration pipelines with standardized cutover runbooks and rollbacks
Industrialized continuous factory: automated discovery, wave orchestration, and telemetry

questions.prompt: Rate your average migration velocity per application group from architecture approval to production:
questions.hint: 1 = Sluggish (>12 months per group); 5 = Industrialized (<1 month per group via self-service).

questions.prompt: Which cloud landing zone automated guardrails are actively enforced in code?
questions.hint: Select all automated baseline controls active across your hyperscaler environments.

options.text: Infrastructure-as-Code (Terraform / OpenTofu / CDK) with Zero Manual Console Changes
Policy-as-Code Guardrails (OPA, AWS Control Tower, Azure Policy) with Drift Detection
Centralized Zero-Trust Transit Hubs & Micro-segmented VPC/VNet Topologies
Automated Tagging Enforcement, Cost Anomaly Alarms & Auto-remediation
Continuous Cloud Security Posture Management (CSPM) & Vulnerability Scanning

questions.prompt: How rigorously are data centre exit savings, stranded assets, and dual-run costs modeled?
questions.hint: Unmanaged bubble/dual-run costs during 18-month migrations frequently erase business case ROI.

options.text: No financial model; business assumes cloud will be cheaper without modeling exit costs
Basic hardware cost comparisons without factoring facility leases, power, or stranded assets
TCO model includes leases and power, but dual-run migration bubble costs are underestimated
Comprehensive multi-year cash flow model tracking lease step-downs, stranded write-offs, and run rates
Dynamic unit-economics FinOps framework linking cloud unit costs directly to business product margins

questions.prompt: Rate the cross-functional alignment between Infrastructure, App Dev, Security, and Finance:
questions.hint: 1 = Siloed hostility; 5 = Product-mode platform squads sharing unified business OKRs.

questions.prompt: Which business metrics are explicitly contracted to modernization outcomes?
questions.hint: Select all executive outcome KPIs measured by C-suite and board.

options.text: Permanent Operating Run-Rate Reduction (EBITDA Expansion)
Product Feature Release Velocity (Cycle Time Reduction)
Mean Time to Recovery (MTTR) & Operational SLA Resilience
Scope 2/3 GHG Carbon Reductions & PUE Sustainability Goals

anomalyProbes.name: Thermal Ceiling vs AI Expansion Paradox
anomalyProbes.finding: You are planning ambitious high-density AI/GPU compute expansion while your facility power utilization is capped (>80%) and cooling infrastructure remains limited to legacy air containment (<12 kW/rack).
anomalyProbes.clarificationQ: How does the organization plan to support modern GPU thermal envelopes (30–80+ kW/rack)?
options: We will restrict AI/GPU compute strictly to high-density colocation or hyperscaler public cloud
We plan a dedicated capital retrofit for specialized liquid/in-row cooling in our primary DC
We are currently reviewing power constraints and require LTM to model our facility power ceilings

anomalyProbes.name: Contractual Cliff vs Migration Throughput Deficit
anomalyProbes.finding: Major facility leases or hardware renewals expire in <12 months, yet your migration factory velocity exceeds 6–12 months per application group.
anomalyProbes.clarificationQ: How will the enterprise avoid catastrophic dual-run penalties or forced lease extension holdovers?
options: We will negotiate temporary 12-month colocation bridge extensions to buy migration runway
We will establish an accelerated LTM Migration Factory to increase migration throughput 3x
We will prioritize aggressive lift-and-shift for non-critical workloads to meet the lease cutoff

anomalyProbes.name: Workload Scale vs 6R Disposition Void
anomalyProbes.finding: Your enterprise operates a substantial application estate, yet less than 20% of applications have an approved 6R modernization disposition.
anomalyProbes.clarificationQ: What framework will determine which workloads are retired, replatformed, or rehosted?
options: We will conduct a 6-week automated discovery sprint with LTM to classify all workloads
Application owners will define dispositions ad-hoc as their migration waves approach
We will default to bulk IaaS rehost and defer refactoring until after cloud cutover

anomalyProbes.name: Sovereign Boundary vs Cloud Gravity Mismatch
anomalyProbes.finding: Proprietary enterprise data and regulated workloads are being considered for public cloud AI without established sovereign boundaries or localized cryptographic controls.
anomalyProbes.clarificationQ: How will compliance (EU AI Act / DORA / statutory data residency) be enforced?
options: We will isolate regulated data within dedicated sovereign on-premises or sovereign cloud enclaves
We rely on contractual DPA agreements with hyperscalers but lack technical cryptographic boundaries
We require an architectural audit to delineate sovereign data boundaries before AI deployment
